title: FBL 0.2 (draft) — Format Binding Language
description: FBL documents ($defs/Document), written by tool engineers, declare how a format maps to a language's model in both directions. The schema also describes the parsed form of an .adp registration ($defs/Registration) and round-trip fixtures ($defs/Fixture). It references DISL's Doc, LocalizedText, Expression and TypeRef.

Name.description: The name of a binding or of a rule: a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens. Rule names are unique within their binding. See section 2.2.

BindingRef.description: A reference to a binding: a URI reference to an FBL document followed by '#' and the binding's name, such as 'structurizr.fbl#workspace', or '#name' for a binding in the same document. See section 2.3.

Regex.description: A regular expression in the subset of RE2 syntax that RE2, .NET, Java and JavaScript read alike: no backreferences and no lookaround; named groups are written (?<name>...). See section 2.5.

Selector.description: A path to entries in a tree family's lossless reading: segments separated by '/', each a key, '*' (any member or item), '**' (any depth) or '{capture}' (any key, bound to the capture's name in CEL as path.capture). An absolute selector starts with '/'; a relative one is resolved against the enclosing entry. In the xml family a segment is an element name, optionally with one attribute test [@NAME='value']. (FBL 0.9) In the grammar family a segment names a rule, an alias or a terminal of the grammar, optionally with one test [path='value'] (section 4.9). See section 4.2.

Document.description: An FBL document: one or more named bindings, each describing how one format maps to a language's model in both directions. The root of every *.fbl file. See section 2.1.

fbl.description: The FBL version the document is written in: 0.1 to 0.17 (draft); 0.3 names the tool type's specification in place of DISL, lets a specification name one binding per format family, and spells a reference to a stored id as by: "id". 0.4 creates and removes the missing levels of a nested container or child mapping. 0.5 defines a scalar's written text, read with read, and adds quoted and fallback to an attribute binding. 0.6 applies an attribute binding's empty rule to an insert as well as to a set. 0.7 adds the bullets family and the drift check before an edit. 0.8 lets an insert of the yaml and json families write a constant. 0.9 adds the grammar family. 0.10 lets one binding serve readings of different metamodels (origins on a rule, resource.byOrigin, one model per origin of one open body), inserts into a yaml flow sequence, gives a refusal its sentence, writes a nested mapping on an add, and adds secondary, {key:lower} and a fixture's template and expectFiles. 0.11 extends the grammar family so that Structurizr DSL is bound in it (comments owned and kept, recovery inside blocks, escapes, absent and positional parts, several nodes for a many attribute, a block written around a first child, views and the statements of the selected view, a view block that can be added, a value gathered from several places), and says how the legacy layout's keys, numbers and stale entries are written. 0.12 extends the grammar family so that the Wardley map's .owm is bound in it (a block brace on the next line, segments in any order, a slot's items and separator, a sidecar id's kind and ordinal, an identity entry that moves with its key), and reads the legacy identities file as the array of {id, kind, key} its tool writes, no longer as an object. 0.13 lets a {node} slot of a many attribute read several items from one node with split, cut at that text, and write a set of them into the node by splices (Structurizr's tags "Extra, More"). 0.14 lets an insert of the yaml and json families add a member to a mapping, under the key the add gives the attribute bound to the capture its rule's at ends in, refusing a missing, empty or duplicate key with refusals.key and refusals.duplicate. 0.15 extends the grammar family so that Turtle is bound in it with no persistence plugin (a slot's selector reaching up and across the tree with .. and +, further slots read with or, a term read through the body's prefix directives with expand, a node's number with ordinal and its name with name, the other sequences of a value's escape, and a body read in the order its entries end). 0.16 extends the grammar family with Turtle's writes (an insert's continues, which continues a statement and replaces its last token, the operation replace-separator, and a remove's parts and whole, which take a part with its separator and the whole statement when it is the last), gives two entries of a rule on one line places of their own, and plans a run of removes bottom-up. 0.17 adds no construct: a host that supports the grammar family at an earlier version than a construct a binding uses may open, read and edit its documents, warning of each construct it does not read and writing no splice that touches the text such a construct governs (section 15.1). See FBL 0.17, section 2.7.

Binding.description: How one format maps to a language's model: the files it claims, its body (a file of one family, or a folder), its reader (declared rules or a persistence plugin), the rules for elements and relations, registration settings and the template of a new body. See section 3.

reader.description: 'declared' when the rules of this binding read and write the body, or the persistence plugin that does (section 11).

readOnly.description: true, or the sentence a host shows as the reason.

comment.description: lines, blocks: a line that matches is a comment, owned by the statement right below it.

unmatched.description: lines, blocks, bullets: a statement no rule matches is kept ('keep', the default) or also reported as fbl.unbound-statement ('report').

sections.description: (FBL 0.7) bullets: the headings whose list items the rules read (section 4.8).

allOf.description: (FBL 0.11) A block rule of the grammar family has at and no line; a block rule's at and insert, a view given as a slot, opens as an object, selectedView, and an attribute binding's create with after, its gather and a slot's escape stand only in a binding of the grammar family (section 4.9).

Claims.description: Which files a binding claims: by extension or name, whether the extension is shared with other formats, the opt-in marker a shared extension requires, what makes a host suggest this reading, and whether a bare file is ever claimed. See section 12.

suggest.description: Substrings of a body's first 64 KiB that make a host propose this reading.

origins.description: The origins of the tool types that read bodies through this binding; a registration's first line names one of them.

readings.description: For a binding several tool types share: per origin, whether a bare body opens as that reading ('bare', at most one) and what makes a host suggest it.

Marker.description: The opt-in marker that makes a file with a shared extension a body of this binding: a root key of a yaml or json body, a prefix of the first line, or a regular expression matched against the first lines. See section 12.2.

oneOf.description: A root key that must be present.
A prefix the first line (after a byte-order mark) must start with.
A regular expression that must match one of the first lines.

Body.description: Where the model is stored: one file of a format family, or a folder. A folder is recognised by the files in it, read file by file, and watched. (FBL 0.9) A body of the grammar family carries its grammar, start rule and recovery. See sections 4 and 10.

grammar.description: (FBL 0.9) grammar: the grammar that reads the body, in ATD grammar notation (ATD section 4), as its text or as a file beside the FBL document. See section 4.9.

start.description: (FBL 0.9) grammar: the grammar's start rule. Default 'start'.

recognise.description: Globs, relative to the folder, that must all, any or none be present.

settle.description: Milliseconds a watched folder must be quiet before it is read again. Default 400.

prefixes.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar: the directives a slot with expand reads a term through, and how a term is written (section 4.9).

declarations.description: The entries that declare a prefix: each a selector from the root, and the slots of the prefix's name and its IRI.

bases.description: The entries that declare a base: each a selector from the root, and the slot of its IRI.

absolute.description: A term written whole: the group value is its IRI.

prefixed.description: A term written under a prefix: the groups prefix and local.

local.description: What a local name must match for an IRI to be written under a prefix.

terminals.description: The terminals whose tokens are terms under a prefix: each needs a declaration in force where it stands, or the body is unreadable.

ordinals.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar: numberings of nodes, by name, which a slot with ordinal reads: the nodes the selectors of at reach, numbered from 0 in document order, a node before the nodes it holds; a token of the terminal same takes the number of an earlier one with its text (section 4.9).

order.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar: closed reads the body's elements in the order their entries end, an entry held by another before it; document, the default, by where they start (section 4.9).

allOf.description: (FBL 0.9) A body of the grammar family carries its grammar, and only such a body carries one (sections 3.2, 4.9).

Family.description: A format family, each with a lossless reading FBL defines: yaml (YAML 1.2), json (RFC 8259), xml (XML 1.0), lines (one statement per line), blocks (statements nested in braces) (FBL 0.7) bullets (list items nested by indentation under named headings) and (FBL 0.9) grammar (the tree an LALR(1) grammar the binding carries reads). See section 4.

GrammarSource.description: (FBL 0.9) A grammar in ATD grammar notation (ATD section 4): its text, or {file}, the name of a .lark file beside the FBL document. Its %import names only files beside the document. See section 4.9.

Recover.description: (FBL 0.9) grammar: read a body that does not parse in part. The start rule's one expansion is unit*; the body is read unit by unit, and text that does not parse as a unit is skipped to the end of the next token of a sync terminal, kept, and reported as fbl.unparsed-text. See section 4.9. (FBL 0.11) With nested, the body is read in part inside the blocks its open and close tokens make too, and with unclosed an ignored terminal's token that does not end with its text is reported as fbl.unclosed-comment.

unit.description: The rule of which the start rule is a repetition.

sync.description: The synchronising terminals: each a terminal's name, or the text of an anonymous string terminal of the grammar.

nested.description: FBL 0.11, section 4.9: read a body that does not parse in part inside its blocks too. open and close are the terminals (or anonymous string terminals) that open and close a block.

unclosed.description: FBL 0.11, section 4.9: ignored terminals whose token must end with the given text; one that does not is reported as fbl.unclosed-comment.

FileRule.description: Which files of a folder subject are read, and by which family. Their entries are matched by the binding's rules whose 'files' name this rule, or handed to the plugin reader. See section 10.2.

readOnly.description: true, or the sentence a host shows as the reason.

PluginReader.description: A persistence plugin that reads the body and plans splices for changes, under the contract of section 11. The plugin is declared in the DISL specification's plugins with provides persistenceFormat.

TextDefaults.description: Conventions for new text where the body offers no evidence: an empty or new body, or an insertion with no neighbour to copy. See section 6.3.

sequenceIndent.description: yaml: whether a block sequence under a key is indented ('indented') or starts in the key's column ('flush').

quote.description: yaml: the quoting used when a new scalar cannot be plain.

Header.description: A version or identity line or key the body starts with, such as 'timeline: 1' or 'causal-loop 1'. A body without it, or with another value, is read and the difference reported, unless 'required' makes it unreadable. See section 5.6.

BlockRule.description: A node or statement that produces no element. blocks: a statement that opens a { } block, such as 'model {' or 'views {', so that element rules can say which blocks they may appear in. (FBL 0.11) grammar: the nodes a selector reaches, such as a view of a workspace. A block rule with 'view' names a view of the body by the value of that group or slot, which a registration's view header selects. See sections 4.7 and 4.9.

at.description: FBL 0.11, grammar: where the rule's entries are (section 4.9). Exactly one of at and line.

line.description: blocks: the statement. Exactly one of at and line.

view.description: The block defines a view of the body, named by this group's value (blocks), or (FBL 0.11) by this slot's value, a {node} or {value} slot (grammar). A registration's view header selects it (section 9.3).

origins.description: FBL 0.11, section 5.1: the readings this block rule is a view for, as origins of the binding's claims.origins, with the meaning origins has on every rule (section 9.3). Absent: every reading.

insert.description: FBL 0.11, grammar: how a new entry of the block rule is written, planned and undone as an element's insert (section 6.2); it produces no element.

SectionRule.description: (FBL 0.7) bullets: a section of the body, the lines after the first heading whose text matches 'heading', up to the next heading with as many '#' or fewer. A rule's 'within' and an insert's 'container' name it. See section 4.8.

ElementRule.description: How entries of the body become elements of one node type, and how new, changed and removed elements are written back. A tree, xml or (FBL 0.9) grammar rule selects entries with 'at'; a lines or blocks rule matches statements with 'line', and a bullets rule statements, or with 'within' the text of list items. See section 5.

within.description: blocks: the rules whose block encloses the statement; '^' is the top level. (FBL 0.7) bullets: the sections whose list items the rule matches.

selectedView.description: FBL 0.11, grammar: the rule matches only the entry of the view the reading shows and the entries inside it (sections 4.9, 9.3). Only in a binding with a block rule that has view (section 14.1).

opens.description: blocks: the statement may open a { } block. (FBL 0.11) grammar: the text that opens a block after the entry's last token, and the closing line, when an add puts a first child into an entry without a block; a line feed in open writes a line ending and the entry's indentation (section 4.9).

caseInsensitive.description: lines, blocks, bullets: match 'line' ignoring the case of ASCII letters.

files.description: Folder subjects: the file rules whose files this rule reads.

origins.description: FBL 0.10, section 5.1: the readings this rule is read for, as origins of the binding's claims.origins. Absent: every reading.

parent.description: Containment: the nearest enclosing entry matched by one of 'rules' is the parent, in DISL slot 'slot'.

readOnly.description: true, or the sentence a host shows as the reason.

RelationRule.description: How entries of the body become relations of one relation type: where the source and target references are, and how relations are written back. See section 5.4.

within.description: blocks: the rules whose block encloses the statement; '^' is the top level. (FBL 0.7) bullets: the sections whose list items the rule matches.

selectedView.description: FBL 0.11, grammar: the rule matches only the entry of the view the reading shows and the entries inside it (sections 4.9, 9.3). Only in a binding with a block rule that has view (section 14.1).

opens.description: blocks: the statement may open a { } block. (FBL 0.11) grammar: the text that opens a block after the entry's last token, and the closing line, when an add puts a first child into an entry without a block; a line feed in open writes a line ending and the entry's indentation (section 4.9).

caseInsensitive.description: lines, blocks, bullets: match 'line' ignoring the case of ASCII letters.

files.description: Folder subjects: the file rules whose files this rule reads.

origins.description: FBL 0.10, section 5.1: the readings this rule is read for, as origins of the binding's claims.origins. Absent: every reading.

parent.description: Containment: the nearest enclosing entry matched by one of 'rules' is the parent, in DISL slot 'slot'.

readOnly.description: true, or the sentence a host shows as the reason.

IdBinding.description: Where an element's id is stored, when it is stored: in a slot of the body ('from'), read from it and written to it when the element is created, or in the registration's identities block keyed by a natural key ('sidecar', section 8.6). How ids are made, derived and whether they are ephemeral is the language's (DISL persistence.ids); without an id binding the id is the one DISL derives. See section 5.3.

sidecar.description: Ids kept in the registration's identities block, keyed by the value of 'key'.

kind.description: (FBL 0.12) The kind an entry of this rule is kept under, in the identities block and in a legacy identities file: the key of an entry is the kind and the natural key together, so that elements of different kinds with the same natural key keep different ids. Without it, the rule's type is the kind (section 8.6).

ordinal.description: (FBL 0.12) The text appended to the natural key of the n-th later entry of the same kind and key, in document order, with {n} replaced by n, from 2 (section 8.6).

Slot.description: Exactly one place in the body a value is read from and written to: a key of a tree entry, an attribute or the text of an xml element (or of its child selected by 'child'), a named group of a lines, blocks or bullets rule, a list item's continuation (bullets), (FBL 0.9) the text of a node of a grammar body's tree, or part of it, or the matching slot of the enclosing entry. A slot given by 'value' is computed by CEL and read-only. See section 5.2.

continuation.description: (FBL 0.7) bullets: the item's continuation, its continuation lines before its first nested item, blank lines between them included, read with their indentation taken off (section 4.8).

node.description: (FBL 0.9) grammar: a selector relative to the entry, whose segments name rules, aliases and terminals ('.' is the entry itself); the value is the text of the first node or token it reaches, in document order (section 4.9). (FBL 0.15) A selector may reach up with '..' and across with '+' (section 4.9).

word.description: lines, blocks, bullets: the value is the first word of the group (words split on whitespace, a double-quoted run being one word) that matches this expression; its named group 'value', if any, is the value.

flag.description: With word: the value is true when such a word is present, and writing false removes it.

match.description: (FBL 0.9) With node: a regular expression with a named group 'value' that the whole text of the node must match; the value is that group, and its span the value's span (section 5.2).

items.description: (FBL 0.12) grammar, on the {node} slot of a many attribute: a map from an item attribute to a {node} slot relative to each node the selector reaches; the attribute is then a list of structured values, one per node, each a map of its item attributes (sections 5.2, 6.3).

separator.description: (FBL 0.12) The text written between two items of an items slot, (FBL 0.13) or of a split slot; ", " when none is given (section 6.3).

split.description: (FBL 0.13) grammar, on a {node} slot of a many attribute: the text at which the slot's value is cut into items; each piece without the white space at its start and end is an item with its own span, and an empty piece is no item. Not beside items, and holding neither character of the slot's escape (sections 4.9, 5.2, 6.3, 14.1).

escape.description: FBL 0.11, section 4.9, grammar, with node: the escapes of a quoted value. Reading replaces with+quote by quote and with+with by with, and keeps with before any other character; writing escapes every quote and with character of the value. (FBL 0.15) With sequences, unicode, writes and requote, a value of a format with more escapes than a quote's.

sequences.description: (FBL 0.15) The other sequences it reads: from the character after with to the one character it stands for (section 4.9).

unicode.description: (FBL 0.15) A code point written after with: from the letter to the number of hexadecimal digits after it (section 4.9).

writes.description: (FBL 0.15) The characters a value writes by their sequence, beside quote and with (section 6.3).

requote.description: (FBL 0.15) A set replaces the whole node the slot reaches, with the value between two of this character (section 6.3).

expand.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar, with node: the node's text is a term, and the value its IRI, read through the body's prefixes and written back through them; true, or {keywords} with the texts that stand for an IRI whatever the directives say (sections 4.9, 6.3).

ordinal.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar, with node: the value is the number of the node the selector reaches in this numbering of the body's ordinals, the slot being absent for a node it does not number; read-only (section 4.9).

name.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar, with node: the value is the name of the node the selector reaches, its rule, alias or terminal; read-only (section 4.9).

separator.description: (FBL 0.12) separator stands beside items, (FBL 0.13) or beside split.

split.description: (FBL 0.13) A slot whose node holds several items is not a slot of structured items.

AttributeBinding.description: A slot bound to one DISL attribute, with what it reads from a scalar and how empty values, numbers, times, scalar style, references and wire values are written. See section 5.2.

continuation.description: (FBL 0.7) bullets: the item's continuation, its continuation lines before its first nested item, blank lines between them included, read with their indentation taken off (section 4.8).

node.description: (FBL 0.9) grammar: a selector relative to the entry, whose segments name rules, aliases and terminals ('.' is the entry itself); the value is the text of the first node or token it reaches, in document order (section 4.9). (FBL 0.15) A selector may reach up with '..' and across with '+' (section 4.9).

word.description: lines, blocks, bullets: the value is the first word of the group (words split on whitespace, a double-quoted run being one word) that matches this expression; its named group 'value', if any, is the value.

flag.description: With word: the value is true when such a word is present, and writing false removes it.

match.description: (FBL 0.9) With node: a regular expression with a named group 'value' that the whole text of the node must match; the value is that group, and its span the value's span (section 5.2).

escape.description: FBL 0.11, section 4.9, grammar, with node: the escapes of a quoted value. Reading replaces with+quote by quote and with+with by with, and keeps with before any other character; writing escapes every quote and with character of the value. (FBL 0.15) With sequences, unicode, writes and requote, a value of a format with more escapes than a quote's.

sequences.description: (FBL 0.15) The other sequences it reads: from the character after with to the one character it stands for (section 4.9).

unicode.description: (FBL 0.15) A code point written after with: from the letter to the number of hexadecimal digits after it (section 4.9).

writes.description: (FBL 0.15) The characters a value writes by their sequence, beside quote and with (section 6.3).

requote.description: (FBL 0.15) A set replaces the whole node the slot reaches, with the value between two of this character (section 6.3).

read.description: (FBL 0.5) yaml, json: what the slot reads from a scalar: 'text', its written text (section 4.1.5), or 'typed', its typed value converted to the attribute's type. Absent: text for a string attribute, typed for every other. See section 5.2.

quoted.description: (FBL 0.5) yaml, read as typed: whether a quoted scalar converts from its written text ('convert') or stays a text that does not convert ('text', the default).

fallback.description: (FBL 0.5) What the attribute is when its slot is present and its value does not convert to the attribute's type; the entry stays readable and the slot's bytes are kept. See sections 5.2 and 7.4.

report.description: Whether fbl.unconverted-value is reported; default true.

reference.description: The value names another entry of the rules 'to', by the value of their attribute 'by', or by their stored id when 'by' is "id"; renaming that entry rewrites it, and removing it cascades where the removed rule says so. See sections 5.2 and 5.7.

absent.description: What setting a value does when its slot is absent from the entry, per family: 'insert' (the default, an insert-key splice) or 'refuse'.

override.description: A second slot that wins on read when present and is removed when the value is written (a formatted text beside a plain one).

secondary.description: FBL 0.10, section 5.2: a second slot read only when the attribute's slot is absent. Writing the attribute writes its slot and removes this one (remove-key). Not with override.

content.description:
xml text slots: 'text' (escaped character data) or 'html-paragraphs' (an HTML body read as plain text, one line per

).

create.description: How a missing child or part that holds the value is written when a value is set (sections 4.9, 5.2).

anyOf.description: Before the first child with this name.
xml: how a missing child element that holds the value is written when a value is set, and where.
(FBL 0.4) yaml, json: on a slot with child, each missing level of the mapping child reaches is created at the end of the level above it, then the key is inserted into the innermost.

FBL 0.11, grammar: how an absent part holding the value is written. emit is its text with {value}; it is written right after the last token of the first attribute of after that is present; with pad, each absent attribute of after before that one is written first, with its own emit and the empty value. See section 4.9.

items.description: An attribute of the same rule.

gather.description: FBL 0.11, grammar: further {node} slots of the same entry whose values follow the first slot's, in document order. Only on a read-only binding of a many attribute (section 14.1).

items.description: (FBL 0.12) grammar, on a {node} slot of a many attribute: a map from an item attribute to a {node} slot relative to each node the selector reaches; the attribute is then a list of structured values, one per node, each a map of its item attributes (sections 5.2, 6.3).

separator.description: (FBL 0.12) The text written between two items of an items slot, (FBL 0.13) or of a split slot; ", " when none is given (section 6.3).

split.description: (FBL 0.13) grammar, on a {node} slot of a many attribute: the text at which the slot's value is cut into items; each piece without the white space at its start and end is an item with its own span, and an empty piece is no item. Not beside items, and holding neither character of the slot's escape (sections 4.9, 5.2, 6.3, 14.1).

readOnly.description: true, or the sentence a host shows as the reason.

refusals.description: FBL 0.10, section 6.4: the sentence a host shows for each refusal this attribute binding causes, as readOnly gives one: empty, a set or an add refused by empty: "refuse"; absent, a set refused by absent.

expand.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar, with node: the node's text is a term, and the value its IRI, read through the body's prefixes and written back through them; true, or {keywords} with the texts that stand for an IRI whatever the directives say (sections 4.9, 6.3).

ordinal.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar, with node: the value is the number of the node the selector reaches in this numbering of the body's ordinals, the slot being absent for a node it does not number; read-only (section 4.9).

name.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar, with node: the value is the name of the node the selector reaches, its rule, alias or terminal; read-only (section 4.9).

or.description: (FBL 0.15) grammar: further slots of the same entry, in order: the first that is present is read when the attribute's own slot is absent, and a set writes it as that slot writes (section 5.2).

not.description: FBL 0.10: secondary is the reverse of override, and an attribute binding takes at most one of them.

separator.description: (FBL 0.12) separator stands beside items, (FBL 0.13) or beside split.

split.description: (FBL 0.13) A slot whose node holds several items is not a slot of structured items.

Insert.description: How a new entry is written: where it goes, where a missing container is created, the order of its keys, and, for text families, the template it is emitted from. Without insert, adding is refused. See section 6.2.

anyOf.description: Before the named key of the container.

create.description: Where a missing container is created, and its text.

anyOf.description: (FBL 0.4) After the last member of the container's parent, creating every missing level above the container first (section 6.2).
Before the named key of the parent.
Right after the named key of the entry.
At the end of the container the selector names.

constant.description: FBL 0.8, section 6.2: keys every new entry of the rule is written with, each with its scalar value, that no attribute supplies; placed by keys, else after the other keys in this map's order. yaml and json only, and not with emit (section 14.1, step 6).

continues.description: (FBL 0.16) grammar: a statement a new entry is written into rather than where place puts it: the last entry at selects in which each slot of same reads the value the add gives its attribute. The statement's last token is replaced by separator, and the new entry, emit, goes on a line of its own after it. See sections 4.9, 6.2, 6.3.

same.description: An attribute of the rule to a {node} slot relative to the statement.

refusals.description: FBL 0.10, section 6.4: the sentence a host shows for each refusal of this insert: when, the add refused because when is false; container, the add refused because the container is missing and the insert has no create; (FBL 0.14) key, a new member's key missing or empty, and duplicate, a new member's key that the mapping already holds (section 6.2).

Remove.description: How an element is removed: which other rules' entries go with it, and whether a container left empty is removed. Without remove, removing is refused. See section 6.2.

parts.description: (FBL 0.16) grammar: the lists an entry is written in, innermost first. The first whose list holds another item names the part that goes, with one separator. See section 6.3.

item.description: A selector relative to the entry reaching the part of it that stands in the list; . for the entry itself.

whole.description: (FBL 0.16) grammar, with parts: a selector relative to the entry reaching the statement that goes when no list of parts holds another item. See section 6.3.

RegistrationSettings.description: What a binding adds to the registration: headers it reads, (FBL 0.7) further blocks it declares, whether a bare body may be positioned without a registration, and legacy sidecars it reads. See section 8.

blocks.description: (FBL 0.7) Further blocks of the registration, by name, in the order they are written after layout: and identities: (sections 8.1, 8.4).

order.description: ordinal (default): entries in the ordinal order of their keys; kept: an entry stands where the edit put it.

keys.description: names (default), or ids: an entry's key is an element's id, pruned when stale and never ephemeral (section 8.5).

history.description: Whether writes to the block are steps of the history (default true, section 7.1).

createOnFirstPlacement.description: The first placement creates the registration beside a bare body, and (FBL 0.7) so does the first change to a setting a declared block keeps (section 8.4).

resource.description: The selector capture a registration's resource header selects, so one body can hold several diagrams (a bundle file with several jobs): capture for every reading, or (FBL 0.10) byOrigin, a capture per reading's origin. Without the header, the first entry in document order is used, per origin (section 8.2).

byOrigin.description: FBL 0.10, section 8.2: the capture per reading's origin; null: readings of that origin select no resource and see every one. An origin not listed selects none. Every origin is one of claims.origins (section 14.1).

legacyLayout.description: A sidecar of positions read, and written back where it was read from: '{base}.layout.json' keyed by view, then id.

legacyIdentities.description: A sidecar of ids read when the registration has no identities: block, and written back while it exists: '{base}.identities.json'. (FBL 0.12) A JSON array of entries {id, kind, key}, matched to the element of that kind with that natural key (section 8.7).

Template.description: The bytes of a new body. Placeholders {name}, {base} and {key} are replaced by the new file's name, its base name, and the base name folded to a key, (FBL 0.10) {key:lower} by that key with every ASCII letter in lower case, and {newid:<rule>} by a new id made by that rule's id strategy; nothing else is interpreted. See section 13.

byOrigin.description: A different template per reading, keyed by the tool type's origin, for a binding several tool types share.

Registration.description: The parsed form of an .adp registration file (section 8): its origin line, the headers, the positions the user placed, and (FBL 0.7) every further block, declared or not. The file itself is lines, not JSON; this is what it means.

blocks.description: (FBL 0.7) Every block besides layout: and identities:, by name, in the order of the file: its entries, key to value, in their order.

Splice.description: One replacement of a byte range: the operation from the catalogue of section 6.1, the file for folder subjects, the UTF-8 byte offsets in the document before the step (start inclusive, end exclusive), and the new text.

file.description: The file the splice writes, for folder subjects (section 10.4) and (FBL 0.10) in a fixture, a file beside its input, named relative to the input's folder: the body a registration names, or a sidecar (section 15.3). Absent: the input, or the subject's file.

Fixture.description: A round-trip fixture: an input body, what reading it yields, and a sequence of edits, each with the splices it must produce and the document after it. Hosts run fixtures against their implementation; CI checks that each step's splices turn the document before it into 'expect' and back. See section 15.3.

template.description: FBL 0.10, section 15.3: the input is the new document the binding's template gives for a file of this name and the reading of this origin (section 13), placeholders replaced; the reading the fixture's read and steps describe is of that origin.

parent.description: (FBL 0.7) The id of the element this one is contained in (section 5.5), or null at the top level. Absent: not compared.

attributes.description: (FBL 0.5) The values read for the attributes named: a JSON string for a text, a JSON number, bool or null otherwise. Attributes not named are not compared.

document.description: (FBL 0.7) The attributes of the document read, as an element's attributes are stated.

edit.description: One change, or (FBL 0.7) the list of changes one transaction makes, planned as one edit (section 15.3).

expectFiles.description: FBL 0.10, section 15.3: the bytes, after the step, of each file beside the input that the step's splices name in their file, by that name. A splice without file is the input's.

Edit.description: A model change in a fixture: add an element or relation (at a position, FBL 0.3), set attributes, remove, move (FBL 0.3), place, change a setting of a declared block (FBL 0.7), or save without change.

slot.description: (FBL 0.5) The parent's slot the element fills, as an add of section 11.2 names it.

oneOf.description: Set attributes of an element or relation.

occurrence.description: (FBL 0.7) Which holder of a duplicated id, by its place in reading order: 2 for the second.
(FBL 0.7) Which holder of a duplicated id, by its place in reading order: 2 for the second.

oneOf.description: Move an element, with everything under it, to a parent (null for the top level) at a position (FBL 0.3; the change of section 11.2).
Place an element in a registration's layout.
(FBL 0.7) Change an entry of a declared block of the registration (section 15.3).

position.description: Where the entry goes in a kept block: at an index, or after or before the entry with that key.

ModelChange.description: One model change a persistence plugin's plan operation receives (and the shapes a declared binding plans, section 6.4): an object whose one key, add, set, remove, move or retype, holds the change's fields. See FBL 0.2, section 11.2.

oneOf.description: Set attributes of an element or relation.
Move an element, with everything under it, to a parent (null for the top level) at a position.
Change the type of an element; attributes are the values after the type's attributeMapping (DISL 9.5).

ChangePosition.description: Where an added or moved element goes among its parent's children in the slot: at an index counted after the element left its old place, or directly after or before a sibling. See FBL 0.2, section 11.2.

TypeRef.description: The name of a type of the tool type's metamodel, as its specification language defines it (section 1.3).

QualifiedId.description: Dot-separated names, hyphens allowed after the first character.

Expression.description: CEL: a string of CEL source, or an object with it, an expected result type and documentation (section 2.4).

Doc.description: Documentation: a LocalizedText (its summary) or an object with a summary, a description, a rationale, examples, links and tags, as the specification languages define it (section 1.3).

LocalizedText.description: A human-facing text: a string, or a map from BCP 47 language tag to string.

RuleOutsideGrammar.description: (FBL 0.11) What a rule of a binding of another family than grammar does not hold: opens as an object, selectedView, and attribute bindings with escape, gather or create with after (section 4.9); (FBL 0.12) nor items or separator (section 5.2); (FBL 0.13) nor split (section 4.9). (FBL 0.15) Nor expand, ordinal, name or or (section 4.9).
